header:
Date: 2026-12-12
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Leah Gomez (Redwood CSM), Alyssa Moore (Novacare Procurement), Dr. Marcus Lee (Novacare CTO), Priya Singh (Novacare Legal), Daniel Park (Novacare Infra)
summary: Procurement onboarding call covering MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, pilot pricing, and vendor onboarding timeline. Redwood to send redlined MSA and security pack; SE to run benchmarks; Novacare to confirm procurement timeline and return legal redlines.
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. I'm Jamie from Redwood Inference, AE. We also have Ravi our SE and Leah from customer success. How's everyone?
[00:06] Alyssa Moore: Hi Jamie, thanks. Busy end of quarter, so appreciate the time.
[00:09] Dr. Marcus Lee: Marcus here, CTO. Quick intro — we're evaluating vendors for inference across some regulated workloads.
[00:14] Priya Singh: Priya from legal, I'll be focusing on the MSA and DPA bits.
[00:17] Jamie Chen: Great. Goal for today is to walk through the commercial and legal checklist — MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, pricing for a pilot, and an onboarding timeline so procurement can get the PO queued.
[00:27] Leah Gomez: Also want to surface the SOC 2 / security materials and onboarding steps so you know what to expect.
[00:32] Alyssa Moore: High level — procurement wants to know if Redwood can meet our data residency and KMS/HSM requirements, what the SLAs look like (uptime, latency), and the pricing bands for the pilot so we can get budget approval.
[00:44] Ravi Patel: Quick technical note — Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. For regulated stuff you can choose VPC/private deployments, and we integrate with customer KMS for key management. For pilot pricing we typically propose a short reserved capacity or a capped hosted test depending on throughput needs.
[00:58] Daniel Park: On the infra side, we need clarity on network egress, VPC peering, and audit logs. Also curious about KV cache behavior with long-running sessions.
[01:07] Ravi Patel: Yup, we can provide audit logs, and KV cache is managed in the runtime — can surface cache hit rates. For VPC we do a private control plane option and can run on-prem in air-gapped if needed, though that's pricier and longer lead time.
[01:22] Priya Singh: On the DPA front — we need explicit language about data at rest, in transit, retention, and subprocessors. We also want breach notification timeline — 72 hours is typical.
[01:31] Jamie Chen: Totally. We have a standard DPA that includes data residency options and 72-hour notification. We'll send the latest DPA with the redlines. If you want specific subprocessor info we can include the registry.
[01:39] Alyssa Moore: Procurement will likely push for a 45 to 60 day payment term but okay to start with standard net 30 during the pilot. Also, any enterprise discount tiers?
[01:47] Jamie Chen: For pilots we often do a one-time pilot pricing that's competitive — we'll include options: hosted-per-token with a cap, or a small reserved pool for predictable throughput. We can put tiered discounts based on commit.
[01:58] Priya Singh: SLA specifics — Novacare requires 99.9% uptime for production APIs and P95 latency targets under X ms, but for pilot we can accept a lower SLO. Do you have an SLA template?
[02:09] Jamie Chen: Yes, our SLA template includes availability, credit calculations, and response times. For dedicated pools we offer higher uptime SLAs and dedicated support. We'll attach the SLA doc.
[02:17] Dr. Marcus Lee: For our clinical workflows latency matters — p95 under 250 ms ideally. Is that realistic?
[02:24] Ravi Patel: It depends on model + seq length + infra. On dedicated GPU pools with optimized kernels we can hit sub-250 p95 for smaller models. For larger LLMs it might be higher. Part of the pilot we'll run benchmarks to see real numbers with your prompts.
[02:38] Daniel Park: Important: can you provide perf numbers with our redacted data or a synthetic workload that mimics ours?
[02:44] Ravi Patel: Yes, we'll run a throughput/latency test using a synthetic workload that matches your token distribution. We'll share logs and a spreadsheet with cost per token and latency breakdowns.
[02:53] Alyssa Moore: From procurement — we need the MSA and DPA to go to legal by next week for routing. Is that feasible?
[02:59] Jamie Chen: We can send redlined MSA + DPA and pricing sheet by Tuesday, 2026-12-15. Does that work?
[03:05] Priya Singh: That timeline works. We'll review and return with markups.
[03:09] Leah Gomez: I'll drop the SOC2 report, security deck, and onboarding checklist today so you can circulate to compliance.
[03:15] Alyssa Moore: Great. Also curious about breach indemnity and liability caps — procurement prefers mutual caps reflective of contract value.
[03:23] Jamie Chen: Standard Redwood MSA has a liability cap tied to fees paid in the prior 12 months, but we're open to discussion for enterprise. We'll flag Priya for that.
[03:33] Priya Singh: Also want to confirm data deletion upon contract termination and proof of deletion — can you provide attestation?
[03:39] Jamie Chen: Yes, we provide deletion attestations and can include export of customer data. For private/on-prem you can control the data lifecycle fully.
[03:46] Dr. Marcus Lee: Any concerns with multi-region fallbacks? We need to ensure PHI doesn't leave region without explicit consent.
[03:53] Ravi Patel: We support region pinning and routing policies. For PHI workloads we recommend private deployments or dedicated regional capacity to avoid cross-region failover unless explicitly allowed.
[04:03] Alyssa Moore: Pricing question — is there an onboarding fee for private deployment?
[04:07] Leah Gomez: For private/on-prem there is typically a setup fee and longer timeline; we'll list estimates in the pricing sheet. Hosted pilots usually have no setup fee.
[04:16] Alyssa Moore: Can you confirm SOC2 scope — infrastructure and app or just infra?
[04:20] Leah Gomez: SOC2 Type II covers infra and app controls; we'll send the report and cover letter.
[04:24] Priya Singh: Want to call out subprocessors again — need visibility into GPU cloud partners if you're using dedicated/some regions.
[04:31] Jamie Chen: We'll include a subprocessors registry. For Dedicated deployments we can often host on the cloud provider you prefer or on our partners.
[04:38] Dr. Marcus Lee: What about monitoring and observability — can we get per-route latency breakdowns and token cost analytics?
[04:44] Ravi Patel: Yes — Redwood Console provides per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, traces, and error analysis. We'll give demo access for the pilot.
[04:52] Alyssa Moore: Okay, so next steps recap? Jamie to send docs by 12/15, Leah to share SOC2/security pack today, Ravi to run benchmark and share results by 12/20, Novacare legal/procurement to review MSA/DPA and return redlines.
[05:06] Jamie Chen: Sounds good. Anything else on procurement side?
[05:09] Alyssa Moore: One last thing — vendor onboarding requires a PO and vendor compliance checklist sign-off. I'll send the onboarding template to Leah after this meeting.
[05:19] Leah Gomez: Perfect. I'll also include a contact list and a proposed kickoff for the pilot once PO is in.
[05:24] Priya Singh: We'll aim to have initial redlines back within a week after receiving docs.
[05:28] Jamie Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the package and schedule the technical benchmark session. Appreciate your time.
[05:34] Dr. Marcus Lee: Thanks all.
[05:36] Alyssa Moore: Thanks.
[05:38] [Recording ends]
notes: Occasional transcription typos: 'Dedicate' seen instead of 'Dedicated', 'KV cash' mis-transcribed in one spot. Speakers occasionally labelled generically in the export; timestamps approximate. References to a pricing spreadsheet and SOC2 attachment were made; links to be included in follow-up email.
